title: Superseded Sensor Supply on Model Change Grants — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Fulfilment Rule
content:
Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program. Sensor supply that Larkfield has already shipped and that is still running when a new written order of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) changes the CGM model is taken off the authorization grant recorded for that order under the payer authorization already in force, by the rule below.

**Rule.** The superseded-supply adjustment replaces the standard deduction for the latest refill's supply that runs past the order date:

- **(a)** when the customer's insulin pump program is not closed, a pump was delivered on it after that refill shipped, and an over-limit justification record is dated on or after that pump delivery, no block is deducted, the justification being the record of the change and the superseded supply being unusable with the new pump;
- **(b)** when the payer authorization is a per-period approval and that supply runs past the order date, one block is deducted for every 30-day block from the order date into which it runs, a part block counted whole;
- **(c)** otherwise the standard deduction applies: one block for each whole 30-day block of that supply after the order date, any remainder of fewer than 30 days dropped.

The blocks this rule gives take the place of the standard deduction.

**Terms used in the rule.**
- *The latest refill* is the most recent refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance on the program; its supply ends on its ship date plus its supply days. The days that supply runs past the order date are the calendar days from the order date (the newest written order's order date) to that end, none when the end does not fall after the order date.
- *The customer's insulin pump program* is the customer's enrollment in the **Insulin Pump Program**; the rule reads that enrollment's status (every status other than closed counts as not closed) and its pump delivery date. A pump delivered "after that refill shipped" has a pump delivery date later than the latest refill's ship date; a delivery on the ship date itself does not meet it.
- *An over-limit justification record* is a clinical document on the CGM program recorded with the purpose over-limit justification; its date is the visit date it documents, and it meets the rule when that date is on or after the pump delivery date.
- *A per-period approval* is a payer authorization (the grant the latest refill drew on) whose units authorized equal the whole 30-day blocks of its own span, from its valid-from date through its valid-through date with both dates counted, multiplied by the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply, which is 1 on every tier (CGM Self-Pay Program 1, CGM Commercial HMO Program 1, CGM Commercial PPO Program 1, CGM Medicare Advantage Program 1, CGM Original Medicare Program 1, CGM Medicaid Program 1).

### Combinations under (a)

| Pump enrollment not closed | Pump delivered after the latest refill shipped | Justification dated on or after the delivery | Rule applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | (a): no block deducted |
| yes | yes | no | (b) or (c) |
| yes | no | yes or no | (b) or (c) |
| no (closed, or no pump enrollment) | either | either | (b) or (c) |

### Hypothetical figures

Illustrative only. Suppose the latest refill's supply runs 46 days past the order date and (a) does not hold.
- Payer authorization a per-period approval: the supply runs into the 1st and the 2nd 30-day block from the order date, so 2 blocks are deducted (46 divided by 30, rounded up).
- Payer authorization not a per-period approval: 1 whole block is deducted (46 divided by 30, remainder dropped).
- A supply running exactly 30 days past deducts 1 block under (b) and under (c); a supply ending on or before the order date deducts none under either.

Suppose instead the Insulin Pump Program enrollment is active, its pump delivery date is three days after the latest refill's ship date, and an over-limit justification record carries a visit date on the delivery date itself: (a) holds and nothing is deducted, whatever the days run past. With the justification dated the day before the delivery, (a) does not hold.
